facts.statement: The genus Onchosaurus was first described by Gervais in 1852.
Onchosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, between 84.9 and 66.043 million years ago.
facts.quote: Onchosaurus is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid fish from the Late Cretaceous (84.9 to 66.043 million years ago).

facts.statement: Fossils of Onchosaurus have been found in Cretaceous sediments across Egypt, Brazil, Congo, Morocco, France, Niger, Japan, Colombia, Chile, Peru, and the United States.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Cretaceous sediments of Egypt, Brazil, Congo, Morocco, France, Niger, Japan, Colombia, Chile, Peru and the United States.

facts.statement: Onchosaurus is known only from isolated vertebrae and rostral spines.
facts.quote: These sclerorhynchid sawskates are only known by isolated vertebra and rostral spines.

facts.statement: Based on fossil evidence, Onchosaurus were large, bottom-dwelling fish that inhabited shallow marine environments but were also capable of powerful swimming.
facts.quote: On the basis of fossil findings they are considered large, bottom-dwelling fishes, mainly inhabiting shallow marine habitats, but they were also powerful swimmers.

facts.statement: Onchosaurus belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae, commonly known as sawskates.
The parent group of the genus Onchosaurus is the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Onchosaurus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for the genus Onchosaurus spans from the Turonian to the Ypresian stages, approximately 93.9 to 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Ypresian (93.9 to 48.07 million years ago)
